polityNote: Somali Democratic Republic / Federal Republic of Somalia, de jure including Somaliland (its own regions are the same five). Atoms are the 18 regions of geoBoundaries SOM ADM1 (2015, OpenStreetMap via Wambacher, ODbL), which carries the north-western five separately (Natural Earth merges them into one Somaliland feature).

sources.title: Statoids — Regions of Somalia (Gwillim Law)
sources.says: ~1982 eight provinces became sixteen regions; 1984-06 Awdal split from Woqooyi Galbeed and Sool from Nugaal.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Administrative divisions of Somalia (rev 1369122785)
sources.says: Middle/Lower Juba, Gedo, Bay, Bakool created 1974–75; in June 1984 Awdal and Sool split off, forming the current 18 regions.

spans.dateNote: Span opens when the 18-region layout is attested (June 1984). The region itself is older (1974–75 per Mukhtar via Wikipedia, ~1982 per statoids); not claimed earlier. De jure through 2019 (the federal government still lists the 18 regions). Nugaal lost Sool in June 1984; Not claimed before June 1984.

unresolved.why: Before scope. Province lines (Alto/Basso Giuba, Benadir, Migiurtinia, Mudugh, Hiiraan, Burao, Hargeisa) do not coincide with region lines throughout, and the date of the 16-region reform is disputed between sources (1974–75 vs ~1982).

statoids yso.html: 36 districts of 1961 with their provinces (much larger than today's 118 districts)
geoBoundaries SOM ADM2 (118 districts, GPEI 2022): no source relates them to the 1961 districts or the provinces of ~1964–1982
